title: India Orders Takedown of 15 Offshore Crypto Platforms Over Laundering Violations
excerpt: The Financial Intelligence Unit issued PMLA notices to exchanges including Weex, XT.com and WhiteBIT and asked for their apps and sites to be blocked in India.
body:
• India's Financial Intelligence Unit has issued non-compliance notices to 15 offshore crypto platforms and asked for their apps and websites to be blocked in India.
  • The platforms — including Weex, Blofin, XT.com, Latoken, WOO X and WhiteBIT — allegedly served Indian users without registering under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
  • Notices were issued under Section 13 of the PMLA, which allows warnings, corrective directions and monetary penalties.
  • The action continues a tightening enforcement drive against offshore exchanges operating in India without FIU registration.

India has ordered 15 offshore cryptocurrency platforms to shut their doors to Indian users, escalating its crackdown on digital-asset businesses operating outside the country's anti-money-laundering framework.

The Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) has issued non-compliance notices to 15 offshore virtual digital asset service providers and sought the takedown of their applications and websites for allegedly operating in the country without meeting requirements under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

Who is affected

The platforms named are Weex, Blofin, Rezorex, Bitunix, DigiFinex, Toobit, XT.com, Latoken, WOO X, Pionex, ChangeNow, SimpleSwap, Fixedfloat, WhiteBIT and Guardarian, according to YourStory's report on the ministry announcement.

FIU-IND issued the notices under Section 13 of the PMLA and has asked for action to remove the platforms' applications and URLs from public access in India — effectively cutting off their Indian user base.

The legal backdrop

Virtual digital asset service providers were brought under the PMLA framework in March 2023. Companies offering exchange between virtual digital assets and fiat currencies, transfer of digital assets, or custody and administration of such assets must register with FIU-IND as reporting entities. The requirement applies to platforms serving Indian users even if they have no physical presence in the country.

Registered entities must comply with obligations around customer due diligence, record-keeping and reporting of suspicious transactions. Under Section 13 of the PMLA, FIU-IND can issue warnings, direct reporting entities to take corrective action and impose monetary penalties for compliance failures.

A continuing enforcement drive

Wednesday's action is not a one-off. Indian authorities have been steadily tightening oversight of offshore crypto platforms catering to domestic users, with FIU-IND previously issuing compliance notices and seeking access restrictions against exchanges operating in India without registration.

The government has consistently maintained that virtual digital assets do not have the status of legal tender in India and has repeatedly cautioned investors about the risks of crypto assets — a stance that has pushed several global exchanges to either register or exit the Indian market.

What it means for users

For Indian crypto users — including NRIs managing India-linked holdings — the message is to stick with FIU-registered platforms. Funds parked on the named offshore exchanges could become difficult to access once app stores and ISPs act on the takedown requests. The broader signal is that New Delhi intends to keep the onus of compliance on platforms, not just users, as it shapes its digital-asset regime.
